source_name: Народна банка на РСМ — Јавни набавки (central bank procurement page)
why_relevant: The central bank is itself a contracting authority and a buyer of payment-system, cash-processing, security-printing and core-IT services. Its procurement page is the highest-value single buyer in this cell for payments infrastructure.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Јавни набавки / Е-јавни набавки
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance owns the Treasury and the state's payment relationships and is the policy owner of procurement. Its own procurement notices plus the archived огласи-и-договори pages cover treasury systems, banking service contracts and PFM IT.

source_name: Министерство за дигитална трансформација — Јавни набавки
why_relevant: Owner of national digitalisation, e-services and e-payment gateway initiatives. Its tenders are the leading indicator for government digital-payment acceptance and identity/e-signature infrastructure that banks and PSPs plug into.

source_name: Град Скопје — Сектор за јавни набавки (and municipal procurement pages generally)
why_relevant: Municipalities are heavy buyers of банкарски услуги (account operation, payment collection, POS acceptance for local fees, parking and transport ticketing). The City of Skopje is the largest single municipal buyer and its page also states the legal publication chain (ESJN, Official Gazette, EU Official Journal).

source_name: Центар за граѓански комуникации (Center for Civil Communications) — procurement monitoring
why_relevant: The main independent watchdog analysing MK procurement: semi-annual monitoring reports, a 'rationality index' comparing prices paid by institutions for identical services, red-flag case studies, and single-bidder statistics. Provides interpretation and anomaly detection that raw ESJN data does not.

source_name: Слободен пристап / АСПИ — FOI request platform and register of information holders
why_relevant: Freedom-of-information channel and register of all public information holders, including the Appeals Commission and BJN. Where a contract document is not published, an FOI request is the lawful retrieval route; the register itself is a clean actor map of public buyers.

source_name: Закон за јавните набавки (Law on Public Procurement) — consolidated texts
why_relevant: Defines thresholds, procedure types, mandatory publication points and exemptions — including how financial services are treated. Necessary to interpret why some banking contracts never appear as open tenders (negotiated/exempt procedures) and to calibrate collection completeness expectations.

source_name: US ITA Country Commercial Guide — North Macedonia: Selling to the Public Sector
why_relevant: English-language orientation to how MK public procurement actually works for foreign vendors — thresholds, portal mechanics, IFI-financed routes and known frictions. Useful onboarding context and a cross-check on the legal reading, refreshed roughly annually.

source_name: Tenderi.mk — commercial MK tender aggregator (subscription)
why_relevant: Commercial MK-language tender aggregator with a paid subscription tier and a browsable tender list; the most likely domestic channel where non-e-nabavki (private/commercial) calls for bids, including bank-issued ones, would be republished.

source_name: eTenderi.mk
why_relevant: MK digitalisation service around tender/contract management; useful as a pointer to how private buyers and suppliers organise bid workflows outside ESJN, and possibly a notice channel.

source_name: OpenProcurements.com — North Macedonia
why_relevant: Structured database of MK tenders, contracting authorities and suppliers (search results cite ~15.5k tenders, ~3.7k suppliers). Even though it indexes public procurement, it is the best mapped register of the SUPPLIER side — the same IT/payments vendors that also serve private banks.

source_name: Јавни повици (javnipovici.mk)
why_relevant: Aggregates calls (jobs, grants, procurements, partnerships) explicitly including the PRIVATE SECTOR as a publisher category — one of the few MK channels where a private company's call for offers can legitimately surface.

source_name: Servisea — Јавни набавки (тендери) alerting service
why_relevant: MK commercial service that notifies companies of active tender notices matched to their activity code; a pointer to how MK suppliers discover opportunities and possibly to non-ESJN notice flows.

source_name: Службен весник на РСМ — ТЕНДЕРИ section
why_relevant: The Official Gazette runs a paid tender-notice section that also carries notices from entities not obliged to use ESJN; a legally-published route where a private buyer (incl. a bank) can advertise a call for offers.

source_name: EBRD Client eProcurement Portal (ECEPP)
why_relevant: Where EBRD CLIENTS — including private MK banks receiving EBRD credit lines — must publish procurement, shortlisting and contract-award notices. This is the single most reliable route by which a private bank's spend becomes publicly traceable.

source_name: EBRD corporate procurement & consultancy notices
why_relevant: EBRD's own consultancy assignments in MK (e.g. bank advisory, digitalisation TA) name the financial-sector counterpart and the winning consultant — an indirect view of what MK banks are being helped to buy.

source_name: NLB Group — Principles of conduct in supplier relations / Supplier Code
why_relevant: Group-level supplier rulebook binding on NLB Banka AD Skopje: sets ESG disclosure, audit and confidentiality requirements on vendors. Tells you the onboarding hurdles and gatekeeping for anyone selling to the MK subsidiary.

source_name: NLB Банка АД Скопје — Кодекс / Code of Conduct (MK site)
why_relevant: Local MK-site rendering of the group code; the entry point to look for a local 'набавки'/'добавувачи' contact or registration route at the largest-tier MK bank.

source_name: Развојна банка на Северна Македонија (MBDP) — Огласи/Набавки
why_relevant: The one MK bank that reliably publishes its own procurement notices, planned procurements and concluded contracts on its site. Acts as a visible benchmark for what a bank in MK buys, and its supplier list is a proxy for the private banks' vendor pool.

source_name: ТИРЗ/ФЕЗ — Програма за развој на добавувачи (supplier development)
why_relevant: State supplier-development programme publishing public calls that map which domestic firms are being qualified as suppliers to large/multinational buyers — a directory-building input for the private supplier ecosystem.

source_name: MacedoniaTenders.com
why_relevant: Foreign commercial aggregator that explicitly claims coverage of PRIVATE tenders sourced from newspapers and individual purchasers' websites — the exact category (private-buyer RFPs) the state portal cannot show.

source_name: TendersInfo — Macedonia government & private tenders
why_relevant: Claims to aggregate from government sites, private bodies and newspapers with daily alerts; second candidate for private-buyer RFP coverage.

source_name: J360 — North Macedonia calls for tenders, public and private contracts
why_relevant: Explicitly advertises 'public and private contracts' for North Macedonia; worth testing as a private-RFP feed.

source_name: BidDetail / TenderDetail / TenderImpulse — North Macedonia tender feeds
why_relevant: Cluster of low-cost international tender resellers indexing MK notices; individually weak but collectively useful for cross-checking whether a given bank-related RFP surfaced anywhere outside ESJN.
